## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. ## Findings

For local Whisper, transcription produces **two** on-disk artifacts, not just note text:

1. **The note markdown** (frontmatter + body) — plain transcript text is written into the note body, and status fields go into frontmatter (`crates/type-core/src/domain/notes.rs:47-52`: `recording_audio_path`, `transcription_status`, `transcription_error`, `transcription_id`, `transcription_updated_ms`). The body is built in `recording_note_body()` (`mod.rs:651-661`) and written via `update_recording_note_status()` (`mod.rs:746-771`).

2. **A separate word-level JSON file next to the audio**, in the Recordings storage folder. `whisper.rs:231-248`:
```rust
/// Save word-level transcription JSON alongside the audio file.
/// e.g. audio-xxxx.webm → audio-xxxx.transcription.json
pub fn save_word_level_json(audio_path: &Path, json_content: &str) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    ...
    let json_path = audio_path.parent()...join(format!("{}.transcription.json", stem));
    fs::write(&json_path, json_content)...
```
This is called from `mod.rs:831-841` only for `TranscriptionMethod::LocalWhisper`, using the full raw JSON (including per-word timestamps) returned by `transcribe_audio_local_whisper` (`whisper.rs:130,218-228`, comment: "Keep the full JSON (including words) as-is for saving").

**Important:** no frontmatter field points to this `.transcription.json` file — `transcription_id` is only populated for AssemblyAI (`mod.rs:843-848`: `TranscriptionMethod::LocalWhisper { .. } => None`). The JSON file's location is derived purely by naming convention from `recording_audio_path` (swap extension for `.transcription.json`), so consumers must reconstruct the path rather than read it from frontmatter.

So after local Whisper completes: the audio file, a plain-text transcript embedded in the note body, and a `<audio-stem>.transcription.json` word-timestamp file all coexist in the Recordings folder — the JSON is discoverable only by filename convention, not via any frontmatter reference.</result>

content.text:
Yes — local Whisper transcription leaves behind more than just the note text.

When a note is transcribed via local Whisper, three things end up on disk in the hidden `Recordings/` folder:

1. **The audio file** itself (e.g. `audio-xxxx.webm`)
2. **The plain-text transcript**, written into the note's markdown body (frontmatter tracks status via `recording_audio_path`, `transcription_status`, etc.)
3. **A word-level JSON file**, `<audio-stem>.transcription.json`, saved right next to the audio — this contains the full raw Whisper output including per-word timestamps

The catch: nothing in the note's frontmatter points to that `.transcription.json` file. It's found purely by filename convention (swap the audio file's extension for `.transcription.json`) — there's no `transcription_id` populated for local Whisper the way there is for AssemblyAI.

So if you're cleaning up recordings/notes manually, deleting the audio file won't remove that companion JSON automatically — you'd need to delete it separately since nothing else references it.
